items.title: Drone attack blamed on guerrillas kills at least three soldiers in Colombia
items.summary: Officials accuse National Liberation Army of launching strike followed by clash inside military compound An attack involving explosives dropped from drones followed by a clash inside a military compound in north-eastern Colombia has killed at least three soldiers and wounded four, Colombia’s army said Saturday. Local authorities blamed the attack late Friday on the rebel National Liberation Army (ELN). It targeted a military unit in the municipality of Ocaña, in the Norte de Santander department, which borders Venezuela. Two soldiers died at the site and a third after receiving medical attention, Colombia’s military said on X. Continue reading...

articles.snippet: 용혜인 성평등가족부 장관 후보자가 최근 5년 동안 1억9000만 원이 넘는 정치자금을 기본소득당 등에 기부하고 약 3600만 원의 근로소득세를 감면받았다는 보도에 대해 반박 자료를 냈다.용 후보자 인사청문회준비단은 5일 오후 설명 자료를 통해 “후보자가 소속 정당에 당비(정치자금 기부금)를 납부한 것은 절세 목적이 아니다”라고 밝혔다.준비단은 “후보자는 소속 정당의 유일한 국회의원으로서 책임감을 갖고 근로소득의 일부를 일반당비로 정기 납부해 왔다”며 “이는 통상적인 정치활동에 해당한다”고 했다.그러면서 “후보자가 경제적 이익을 목적으로 했다면 세액공제가 아닌 당비 납입액을 상당수 줄이는 것이 경제적으로 합리적일 것”이라고 덧붙였다.준비단은 “적법한 당비 납부와 소득세법에서 정한 세액공제를 ‘꼼수절세’로 규정한 것은 부적절하며 사실과도 다르다”며 “앞으로도 후보자의 의정활동과 세금 납부와 관련한 자료를 투명하게 공개하고 제기되는 의혹에 성실하게 설명하겠다”고 했다.

articles.title: 네팔 홍수 ‘9일만의 기적’… 발전소 터널서 2명 구조
articles.snippet: 히말라야 산악지대의 대규모 돌발 홍수가 발생한 지 9일 만인 4일(현지 시간) 네팔 트리슐리 3A 수력발전소 터널에서 네팔인 직원 2명이 구조됐다. 연락이 두절된 한국인 직원 9명이 근무해온 어퍼트리슐리(UT)-1 수력발전소와 직선거리로 약 6km 떨어진 곳이다. 가까운 발전소에서 극적인 생존자 구조 소식이 전해지면서 한국인 등 추가 생존자에 대한 구조 기대감이 높아지고 있다. 이날 비라지 박타 슈레스타 네팔 에너지장관, 수단 구룽 네팔 내무장관에 따르면 트리슐리 3A 수력발전소 터널에서 네팔인 기계반장과 기계감독관 등 2명이 구조됐다. 이 외 숨진 근로자 1명도 같은 터널에서 발견됐다. 네팔 현지 방송에선 진흙투성이의 해당 직원들이 구조대원의 어깨에 들려 구조되는 모습이 방영됐다. 구조된 2명은 네팔 수도 카트만두 병원으로 옮겨져 치료를 받고 있다. 수력발전소 관련 실종자는 현재까지 945명으로, 이 중 한국인 직원들이 근무해 온 UT-1 수력발전소에서만 557명이 실종됐다.

articles.title: The pressure on Burnham to appease the right is huge. But now is the time to step out of Reform’s shadow | Andy Beckett
articles.snippet: A scandal-besieged Reform still has a loyal base that won’t budge. That should free up the PM to deliver some home truths Despite the bright start to Andy Burnham’s premiership, and Reform UK’s sudden disarray, a shadow still hangs over British centre-left politics. Labour has a small poll lead, a cautious air of confidence and a leader who seems energised rather than overwhelmed by trying to solve the country’s problems. Meanwhile, Reform is having a terrible 2026: mired in deepening funding scandals, losing winnable byelections and, thanks to the drama and novelty of Burnham’s leadership coup and new government, no longer the freshest story around. Yet Reform UK’s support has either held up or fallen only slightly in most polls since Burnham entered Downing Street. Even in the Makerfield byelection, where he beat it more decisively than expected, Reform’s vote share and total support actually rose. Nigel Farage may have spent the year uncharacteristically avoiding journalists, or in his prickly rather than jolly public mode, but the overwhelming majority of Reform supporters, almost a quarter of the electorate, remain faithful. “Power is within our grasp!” insisted Zia Yusuf, Reform’s home affairs spokesman, at its party conference in Birmingham on Friday, and they applauded with determined gusto. articles.title: The Guardian view on Reform’s funding scandal: Nigel Farage has questions to answer | Editorial
articles.snippet: An undercover investigation raises issues around foreign money, political transparency and the rightwing populist party’s fitness for power Reform UK’s conference was to open showcasing a party ready for government. It did so with two top aides removed after an investigation aired on Channel 4, its finances under police scrutiny and seven in 10 voters, polls suggest, regarding its leader, Nigel Farage, as sleazy – double the number who thought the same of Andy Burnham. Reform, a rightwing populist party, says it will take power back from a corrupt establishment. The latest scandal raises a question: does Reform oppose the influence of big money – or just who benefits from it? Undercover reporters from Verbatim Investigations, founded by journalists from the Centre for Climate Reporting, pretended to be a wealthy American father and his UK-based son who wanted to donate to Reform. In the UK, foreign donations are banned from politics. But that allegedly was ignored. Verbatim’s team filmed their meetings with James Orr, a Cambridge academic specialising in ethics, and Reform’s head of policy, as well as with Dan Jukes, Mr Farage’s close aide.
